item.title: Dire Vulture
item.description: The dire vulture is a moderate annoyance for well-equipped desert travelers, but a frightful scourge for the less fit.Beak (16): 1d pi+; Reach C, 1. Claws (16): 1d-1 cut; Reach C. Traits: Cowardice (12); Kleptomania (12); Striking ST 2 (Beak only); Wild Animal. Skills: Brawling-16; Intimidation-10; Stealth-10. Class: Dire Animal. Notes: Dire vultures can parry with their iron-hard beaks. They will flee after losing half their HP. However, they are very good a spotting the weak and vulnerable and will focus their attacks accordingly. They will attack the least heavily armored targets and may, on a successful Per roll, notice recent wounds as well. Instead of striking for damage, they may, on a failed Kleptomania roll, grab at a prominent interesting object (a helmet, a jeweled staff, etc.) and try to fly off with it.“Pasted image 20220127132811.png” could not be found.

item.title: Gibbering Mouther
item.description: Infobox The gibbering mouther is an amorphous mass of mouths and eyes. It can use only six mouths at the same time, and can create protoplasmic manipulators to push objects (hence No Fine Manipulators, not No Manipulators). It can spit acid, soften earth, confuse creatures with its gibbering, and attack six times per second. It has so many eyes that it effectively has Injury Tolerance (No Eyes).Gibbering Mouther [Monster Manual, page 126]Vampiric Bite (12): 1d+1 cutting (KYOS: 2d cutting), Reach C. The gibbering mouther can drain the victim’s life if the victim is helpless (pinned, stunned, unconscious, etc.), grappled, or willing. If he is wearing armor, the gibbering mouther’s biting damage must penetrate its DR. Once the gibbering mouther has bitten through the victim’s DR, it can drain 1 HP per second from him. For every 3 HP stolen, the gibbering mouther heals 1 HP or 1 FP (its choice). It cannot raise its HP or FP above normal this way.Spit Acid (12): 1d-1 corrosion. Ranged attack (Acc 3, Range 10/10), costs 1 FP.Gibbering: As soon as a mouther spots something edible, it begins a constant gibbering. When a creature hears this gibbering, it must roll a Fright Check using the Confusion table (GURPS Powers, p. 85). If a victim succeeds at his Fright Check, he will be unaffected by this ability for one hour.Ground Manipulation: A gibbering mouther can cause stone and earth in a 4-yard radius around it to become a morass akin to quicksand. This requires a Concentrate maneuver and costs 1 FP. Mired creatures are grappled with ST 12. Their only way to free themselves is to break free with a successful Quick Contest of ST. Softening stone requires two consecutive Concentrate maneuvers. This effect persists for 10 seconds.                Traits: 360° Vision; Constriciton Attack; Disturbing Voice; Extra Attack 5; Extra Mouth 5; Horizontal; Immunity to Ground Manipulation; Infravision; Injury Tolerance (Damage Reduction 2; Limited, Crushing); Injury Tolerance (Homogenous, No Blood, No Eyes, No Head, No Neck); Invertebrate; No Fine Manipulators; No Legs (Slithers).Skills**:** Brawling-12; Innate Attack (Breath)-12.Creature Type**:** Aberration.Notes**:** Size 2 hexes; Weight 200 lbs.356 pointsAttribute Modifiers: ST+5 (No Fine Manipulators, -40%) [30]; IQ-4 [-80]; HT+3 [30].Secondary Characteristic Modifiers: Will+4 [20]; Per+4 [20]; Basic Move -2 [-10].Advantages: 360° Vision [25]; Amphibious [10]; Constriction Attack [15]; DR 2 (Can’t Wear Armor, -40%; Tough Skin, -40%) [2]; Extra Attack 5 [125]; Extra Mouth 5 [25]; Infravision [10]; Injury Tolerance (Damage Reduction 2; Limited, Crushing, -40%) [30]; Injury Tolerance (Homogenous, No Blood, No Eyes, No Head, No Neck) [62]; Vampiric Bite [30].Gibbering: Terror 1 (Confusion; Hearing; Magical, -10%) [27].Ground Manipulation: Binding 12 (Area Effect, 4 yards, +100%; Costs 1 FP, -5%; Emanation, -20%; Environmental, Earth or Stone, -40%; Magical, -10%; Persistent, +40%; Takes Extra Time 1 for Stone, -5%; Unbreakable, +40%) [48].Spittle: Corrosion Attack 1d-1 (Blockable, -5%; Costs 1 FP, -5%; Increased 1/2D, x10, +15%; One-Shot, -10%; Reduced Range, 1/10, -30%) [6].Disadvantages: Disturbing Voice [-10]; Horizontal [-10]; Invertebrate [-20]; No Fine Manipulators [-30].Perks: Immunity to Ground Manipulation [1].Features: No Legs (Slithers) [0].Creature Type: AberrationNotes: Size 2 hexes; Weight 200 lbs.Knowing Your Own Strength [376]Replace ST+5 (No Fine Manipulators, -40%) [30] with ST+5 [50]

item.title: Gnome
item.description: The gnomes in D&D are small humanoids with minor magical powers, in Pathfinder they also are migrants from the First World, the world of the fey. While interesting, I've never seen a person play a gnome, and even use gnome as an NPC. I think gnomes are the most overlooked "core" race.ROCK GNOME [-24] (Player’s Handbook, page 16)Attributes: ST-5 [-50]; HT+1 [10].Secondary Characteristics: SM -2; FP +1 [3]; Basic Move -1 [-5].Advantages: Acute Hearing 1 [2]; Acute Taste and Smell 1 [2]; Extended Lifespan 2 [4]; Night Vision 5 [5].Light: Illumination (2-yard radius, 1 minute; Limited Use, 1/day, -40%; Magical, -10%) [1].Sound: Illusion (Auditory only, -70%; Limited Use, 1/day, -40%; Magical, -10%) [5].Burrowing Animal Speech: Speak with Animals (Burrowing animals only, -60%; Magical, -10%) [8].Perks: Intuitive Illusionist [1].Rock gnomes are the "standard" gnomes. They possess minor magical abilities that allow them to create light, sound, and talk to burrowing animals. While the first two abilities are useful, they can only be used once per day.SVIRFNEBLIN (DEEP GNOME) [96] (Monster Manual, page 132)Attributes: ST-5 [-50]; DX+1 [20].Secondary Characteristics: SM -2; FP +1 [3]; Basic Move -1 [-5].Advantages: Acute Hearing 1 [2]; Acute Taste and Smell 1 [2]; Extended Lifespan 2 [4]; Infravision [10]; Magic Resistance 2 (Improved, +150%) [10]; Night Vision 5 [5].                Nondetection: Obscure 10 (Divination; Defensive, +50%; Stealthy, +100%; Always On, -50%; No Area of Effect, -50%; Magical, -10%) [28].Disguise Self: Morph (Illusory; Cosmetic, -50%; Costs 1 FP, -5%; Magical, -10%) [40].Blur: Obscure 2 (Vision; Defensive, +50%; Extended, Infravision, +20%, Stealthy, +100%; Costs 1 FP, -5%; Limited Use, 1/day, -40%; Magical, -10%) [9].Strike Blind: Affliction 1 (Disadvantage, Blindness, +50%; Limited Use, 1/day, -40%; Magical, -10%) [10].Strike Deaf: Affliction 1 (Disadvantage, Deafness, +20%; Limited Use, 1/day, -40%; Magical, -10%) [7].Perks: Intuitive Illusionist [1].Svirfneblins are a subrace that actually gets some attention outside Monster Manual. They are one of the few "good" races of the underground world, and they posess much more powerful abilities than the other subraces.FOREST GNOME [1] (Monster Manual, page 132)Attributes: ST-5 [-50]; HT+1 [10].Secondary Characteristics: SM -2; FP +1 [3]; Basic Move -1 [-5].Advantages: Acute Hearing 1 [2]; Acute Taste and Smell 1 [2]; Extended Lifespan 2 [4]; Night Vision 5 [5].Light: Illumination (2-yard radius, 1 minute; Limited Use, 1/day, -40%; Magical, -10%) [1].Sound: Illusion (Auditory only, -70%; Limited Use, 1/day, -40%; Magical, -10%) [5].Beast Speech: Speak with Animals (Magical, -10%) [23].Perks: Intuitive Illusionist [1].Suprisingly, the forest gnomes also do get some attention in Races of Faerun. Their ability to talk to animals is not limited to burrowing animals.STONEHUNTER GNOME [-15] (Dragon Magic, page 8)Attributes: ST-5 [-50]; HT+1 [10].Secondary Characteristics: SM -2; FP +1 [3]; Basic Move -1 [-5].Advantages: Acute Hearing 1 [2]; Acute Taste and Smell 1 [2]; Extended Lifespan 2 [4]; Night Vision 5 [5].Light: Illumination (2-yard radius, 1 minute; Limited Use, 1/day, -40%; Magical, -10%) [1].Sound: Illusion (Auditory only, -70%; Limited Use, 1/day, -40%; Magical, -10%) [5].Burrowing Animal Speech: Speak with Animals (Burrowing animals only, -60%; Magical, -10%) [8].Blood of the copper dragons flows in stonehunter gnome's veins. They lose their Intuitive Illusionist perk, and... that's it. ICE GNOME [-22] (Frostburn, page 35)Attributes: ST-5 [-50]; HT+1 [10].Secondary Characteristics: SM -2; FP +1 [3]; Basic Move -1 [-5].Advantages: Acute Hearing 1 [2]; Acute Taste and Smell 1 [2]; Extended Lifespan 2 [4]; Night Vision 5 [5].Ray of Frost: Fatigue Attack 1d (Freezing, +20%; Limited Use, 1/day, -40%; Magical, -10%) [7].Light: Illumination (2-yard radius, 1 minute; Limited Use, 1/day, -40%; Magical, -10%) [1].Arctic Animal Speech: Speak with Animals (Arctic animals only, -60%; Magical, -10%) [8].Perks: Intuitive Illusionist [1].The ice gnomes live in harsh environments, but do not posess any Temperature Tolerance. But they gain the ability to project a ray of frost once a day.AQUATIC GNOME [9] (Unearthed Arcana, page 7)Attributes: ST-5 [-50]; HT+1 [10].Secondary Characteristics: SM -2; FP +1 [3]; Basic Move -1 [-5].Advantages: Acute Taste and Smell 1 [2]; Amphibious [10]; Extended Lifespan 2 [4]; Night Vision 5 [5]; Pressure Support 1 [5]; Speak Underwater [5].Light: Illumination (2-yard radius, 1 minute; Limited Use, 1/day, -40%; Magical, -10%) [1].Sound: Illusion (Auditory only, -70%; Limited Use, 1/day, -40%; Magical, -10%) [5].Aquatic Animal Speech: Speak with Animals (Aquatic animals only, -40%; Magical, -10%) [13].Perks: Intuitive Illusionist [1].Features: Doesn’t Breathe (Gills) [0].And let's start with the good ol' environmental variants. DX+1 [20].Secondary Characteristics: SM -2; FP +1 [3]; Basic Move -1 [-5].Advantages: Acute Hearing 1 [2]; Acute Taste and Smell 1 [2]; Doesn’t Breathe [20]; Extended Lifespan 2 [4]; Night Vision 5 [5].Light: Illumination (2-yard radius, 1 minute; Limited Use, 1/day, -40%; Magical, -10%) [1].Sound: Illusion (Auditory only, -70%; Limited Use, 1/day, -40%; Magical, -10%) [5].Bird Speech: Speak with Animals (Birds only, -50%; Magical, -10%) [10].Disadvantages: Susceptible to Earth Spells (-3) [-3].Perks: Intuitive Illusionist [1].In real life mythology, gnomes are earth spirits. You would think the authors of Unearthed Arcana would create earth gnomes as the elemental gnomish subrace?WAVECREST GNOME [-9] (Stormwrack, page 44)Attributes: ST-5 [-50]; HT+1 [10].Secondary Characteristics: SM -2; FP +1 [3]; Basic Move -1 [-5].Advantages: Absolute Direction [5]; Acute Hearing 1 [2]; Acute Taste and Smell 1 [2]; Extended Lifespan 2 [4]; Night Vision 5 [5].Light: Illumination (2-yard radius, 1 minute; Limited Use, 1/day, -40%; Magical, -10%) [1].Aquatic Animal Speech: Speak with Animals (Aquatic animals only, -40%; Magical, -10%) [13].Perks: Intuitive Illusionist [1].And the last one of the environmental variants. The wavecrest gnomes cannot get lost and cannot create auditory illusions.CHAOS GNOME [13] (Races of Stone, page 86)Attributes: ST-5 [-50]; DX+1 [20]; HT+1 [10].Secondary Characteristics: SM -2; FP +1 [3]; Basic Move -1 [-5].Advantages: Acute Hearing 1 [2]; Acute Taste and Smell 1 [2]; Extended Lifespan 2 [4]; Luck (Active, -40%; Game Time, +0%) [9]; Night Vision 5 [5].Light Jet: Illumination (narrow 10-yard beam, 1 minute; Limited Use, 1/day, -40%; Magical, -10%) [1].Daze: Affliction 1 (Based on Will, +20%; Limited Use, 1/day, -40%; Magical, -10%) [7].Missile Shield: DR 5 (Ranged Attacks, -20%; Force Field, +20%; Active Defense, -40%; Limited Use, 1/day, -40%; Magical, -10%) [5].The chaos gnomes have a totally different array of magical abilities. Lore-wise they seem to be much closer to the Pathfinder gnomes than the rock gnomes.WHISPER GNOME [32] (Races of Stone, page 94)Attributes: ST-5 [-50]; DX+1 [20]; HT+1 [10].Secondary Characteristics: SM -2; FP +1 [3]; Per +1 [5].Advantages: Extended Lifespan 2 [4]; Infravision [10]; Night Vision 5 [5]; Silence 3 [15].Silence: Obscure 10 (Hearing; Limited Use, 1/day, -40%; Magical, -10%) [10].Sound: Illusion (Auditory only, -70%; Limited Use, 1/day, -40%; Magical, -10%) [5].Apportation: Telekinesis 1 (Magical, -10%) [4].Perks: Ping [1].Whisper gnomes actually are quite interesting. item.title: Green Slime
item.description: This dungeon peril is a dangerous variety of normal slime. Green slime devours flesh and organic materials on contact and is even capable of dissolving metal. Bright green, wet, and sticky, it clings to walls, floors, and ceilings in patches, reproducing as it consumes organic matter. It drops from walls and ceilings when it detects movement (and possible food) below.A single 5-foot square of green slime deals 1d-2 corrosion damage (minimum 1 point) per round while it devours flesh. On the first round of contact, the slime can be scraped off a creature (destroying the scraping device), but after that it must be frozen, burned, or cut away (dealing damage to the victim as well). Anything that deals cold or fire damage, sunlight, or a Cure Disease spell destroys a patch of green slime. Against wood or metal, green slime deals 1d-2 points of corrosion damage per round, ignoring metal’s hardness but not that of wood. It does not harm stone.

item.title: Harpy
item.description: open outsideHarpies appear to be half woman, half bird. In fact, there’s nothing human about them at all – they aren’t sapient, don’t use tools, and don’t speak. Though they have no hands, their feet sport large claws. They’re usually encountered in groups of five or more, active day or night. They are most commonly found in the badlands of al-Haz and al-Wazif or in mountainous areas of the Great Forest and the Emperor’s Forest.Harpies take a bizarre, compulsive delight in befouling food and drink; the stench they leave sends most other beings reeling, and the food will be completely inedible. Otherwise, they act much like aggressive predatory animals, with neither a fear of humans nor any great interest in human prey. They will rarely harm anyone not in their way, but will viciously attack anyone who is. People wounded by a harpy’s claws must roll for infection (p. B444); treat this as a wound with infected matter in it.Harpies usually attack with their claws from above (often striking for opponents’ heads). They are less effective fighters on the ground; their Dodge falls to 6.ST 12; DX 13; IQ 5; HT 13.Will 10; Per 12; Speed 6.5; Dodge 10;Move 3.SM +0 (1 hex); 150 lbs.Traits: Bad Temper (9); CombatReflexes; DR 1; Enhanced Move1/2 (Air Speed 19); Flight (Winged;Air Move 13); No Fine Manipulators;Sharp Claws; Wild Animal.Skills: Brawling-15.

item.title: Mimic
item.description: Mimics are classic D&D monsters that exude adhesive slime and fool adventurers by pretending to be chests, doorframes, beds, and other objects.Mimic [Monster Manual, page 186]Pseudopod (14): thrust 1d+1 crushing (KYOS: 2d+1 crushing) + adhesive. Reach C-1.Adhesive: A mimic exudes a thick slime that acts as a powerful adhesive, holding fast any creatures or items that touch it. Adhesive has ST 12 and can only be damaged by cutting or burning attacks. Strong alcohol dissolves the adhesive, but the mimic still can grapple normally. A mimic can dissolve its adhesive at will, and the substance breaks down 30 seconds after the creature dies. See Binding, p. B40 for more details.Mimic Shape: A mimic can assume the general shape of any object that fills roughly 150 cubic feet (5 feet by 5 feet by 6 feet), such as a massive chest, a stout bed, or a wide door frame. The creature cannot substantially alter its size, though. A mimic’s body is hard and has a rough texture, no matter what appearance it might present. Anyone who examines the mimic by touch can detect the ruse by making a successful Touch roll. Of course, by this time it is generally far too late.The mimic can always take on the form of an object he can see or touch. Once it have assumed a form, it can opt to memorize it by concentrating for one minute. This allows the mimic to shapeshift into that form at any time. It can memorize a number of forms equal to its IQ. If all its “slots” are full, it must overwrite a previously memorized form (its choice) to add the new form.                Traits: 360° Vision; Constriction Attack; Extra-Flexible Arms; Double-Jointed; Immunity to Noxious Acidic Effects; Infravision; Injury Tolerance (No Eyes; No Head; No Neck; No Vitals); Internal Sealed (Acid-Resistant Only); Invertebrate; No Legs (Slithers); Reduced Consumption 4; Sealed (Acid-Resistant Only); Universal Digestion.Skills**:** Brawling-14; Disguise/TL3 (Objects)-15; Wrestling-14.Creature Type**:** Aberration (Shapechanger).Notes**:** Size 2 hexes; Weight 4,500 lbs.307 pointsAttribute Modifiers: ST+6 (Size Modifier, -10%) [54]; HT+2 [20].Secondary Characteristic Modifiers: SM+1; Basic Move-4 [-20].Advantages: 360° Vision [25]; DR 1 (Tough Skin, -40%) [3]; Constriction Attack [15]; Extra-Flexible Arms [10]; Double-Jointed [15]; Infravision [10]; Injury Tolerance (No Eyes; No Head; No Neck; No Vitals) [22]; Reduced Consumption 4 [8]; Universal Digestion [5].Acid Resistance [58]: DR 20 (Includes Internal, +20%; Limited, Acid, -40%; Tough Skin, -40%) [40] + Immunity to Noxious Acidic Effects [10] + Internal Sealed (Acid-Resistant Only, -60%) [2] + Sealed (Acid-Resistant Only, -60%) [6].Adhesive: Binding 12 (Aura, +80%; Melee Attack, Reach C, -30%; One-Shot, -10%; Only Damaged by Burning and Cutting, +20%; Terminal Condition, Alcohol, -10%) [36].Mimic Shape: Morph (Cosmetic, -50%; Reduced Time 1, +20%; Unliving Forms Only, -0%) [70].Disadvantages: Invertebrate [-20].Features: No Legs (Slithers).Notes: Size 2 hexes; Weight 4,500 lbs.Creature Type: Aberration (Shapechanger).Knowing Your Own Strength [313]Replace ST+6 (Size Modifier, -10%) [54] with ST+6 [60]

item.title: Mind Flayer
item.description:
Infobox Mind flayers, also known as illithids, are iconic D&D monsters. They have powerful telepathic abilities and their signature brain extraction move. Avoid them, unless you have prepared mental defenses. I suggest reading Lords of Madness for D&D 3.5 or The Illithiad for AD&D 2e. Both are great reads. Mind Flayer (Illithid) [Monster Manual, page 186, Expanded Psionics Handbook, page 204]Punch (11): thrust 1d-2 crushing. Reach C.Tentacles (11): The mind flayer has four short tentacles that encircle its mouth. These cannot manipulate objects, but the mind flayer can use them to attack, as if biting. This deals 1d-2 large piercing damage. The mind flayer has a +2 to its effective SM for the purpose of determining how it can bite (see GURPS Martial Arts, p. 115). Typically, the mind flayer targets the skull with its tentacles and worries (worrying deals 2d-1 large piercing damage), trying to extract the brain. item.title: Rakshasa
item.description:
Infobox Let's go back to converting monsters, there aren't that many left in the Monster Manual for D&D 3.5. This post details the rakshasa - an innately magical shapeshifting/mindreading tigerman. Also, I decided to also add the description of their racial deity Ravanna from the Dragon Magazine #326. The deity's portfolio is very similar to the scope of rakshasas innate spellcasting, so why would a rakshasa worship their own racial deity? item.title: Strige
item.description: open outsideStirges are bird-like creatures that drink the blood of their victims for sustenance. They have four small, pincer-like legs that they use to clamp onto the necks of their victims. They are rusty-red to reddish brown in color, and their eyes and feet are yellowish. The dangling proboscises of stirges are pink at the tip, fading to gray at the base (near their heads). Stirges must be killed to be removed, due to their strong grip. If an attack against an attached stirge misses, make another attack roll against the victim’s Armor Class to see if the attack hits the victim instead. Caution is advisable when attempting to remove an attached stirge.Stirges can breed in captivity, but a constant supply of blood is needed. Stirges mostly kill low-level humans, animals and children, so the arrival of these predators in any civilized territory is always a cause for alarm. Fortunately, even a low-level group of adventurers or town militia is usually capable of ending the menace with little or no loss of life.Ecology: Stirges have an acute sense of smell, can see in the dark, and can sense heat sources within 200 feet. These senses keep stirges informed when living creatures enter their habitat. Creatures with a natural AC of 3 or better are usually immune to a stirge’s blood draining attack, since their hides are too thick to penetrate. As a consequence, huge nests of stirges live symbiotically with some evil dragons. Characters who protect their entire bodies with special leather or better armor (this special armor costs two to three times more than normal armor) can safely approach a stirge. Even the slightest gap in the protection is seen and smelled by the creature, and a successful attack roll means the creature has broken through the weakness and locked on. After a stirge has gorged itself by draining blood, it sleeps for one day, plus one day for every 2 points of blood it drank (the maximum sleep period is after drinking 12 points of blood – seven days). During this period of rest, silent attackers can impose a -2 penalty to the stirges’ surprise roll, as the beasts wake slowly and remain drowsy for a few moments. They are most vulnerable at this time. While certain species of stirges prefer to dine on human blood, most are content with any large mammal, like cows, moose, and deer. Experienced druids and rangers usually recognize the traces of a stirge colony by the occurrences of mysteriously drained and dead animals in the vicinity. A stirge colony’s territory extends for only a mile in diameter, so stirges move around a lot after they’ve drained a region of the available blood. Often, the presence of stirges is only discovered long after the colony has departed, making it very difficult to track them.ST 5; DX 15; IQ 4; HT 11.Will 10; Per 10; Speed 6.5; Dodge 9; Move 2 (ground); 12 (air). SM-5; HP 7 (): Grappling (17); Innate Attack [piercing] (17); Damage: 1d-2; If the proboscis penetrates the victim’s DR, the stirge drains 1 HP per second from him. For every 3 HP stolen, the stirge heals either 1 HP or 1 FP. The stirge cannot raise HP or FP above normal this way. A stirge is vulnerable when feeding in this manner and will be unable to dodge any attack directed at it. A missed attack, however, may hit the stirge’s victim! (additional per round) Traits: Flight (Winged; Air Move 12) [+30]; Night Vision 5 [+5]; Striker (Cannot Parry) [+3]; Vampiric Bite [+30];Bloodlust [-10]; No Fine Manipulators [-30]; Wild Animal [-30]. . Skills:Stealth-15 [+2]. Class: Combat Effectiveness Rating: Notes:

item.title: Xill
item.description:
Xills are four-armed humanoid outsiders that lurk on the Ethereal Plane and attack unwary prey on the other planes.Xill [Monster Manual, page 259]Typical StatsSharp Teeth (14): 1d-1 cutting plus follow-up affliction (resisted by HT, paralysis for margin of failure hours, then physical stun). Reach C.Sharp Claws (14): 1d-1 cutting. Reach C.Shortsword (14): swing 1d+1 cutting, Reach 1 or thrust 1d impaling, Reach 1.Longbow (14): 1d+1 impaling, Acc 3, Range 165/300, RoF 1, Shots 1(2).
Implant: A xill that deals injury with a bite attack can inject an egg pellet into the opponent’s body. The affected creature must make a successful HT-3 roll to avoid implantation. Often the xill implants an unconscious or otherwise helpless creature. The egg gestates for 90 days, then the host takes 2d toxic damage each hour for 13 cycles. Each cycle allows an additional HT-3 roll that prevents any further damage and destroys the egg pellet. Once the host loses 1/2 of their HP to this effect, they begin experiencing terrible pain (p. B428) until they heal above that threshold. Once the host loses 2/3 of their HP to this effect, they begin experiencing agony (p. B428) until they heal above that threshold. The egg pellet can be removed with a successful Surgery roll (failure deals 1d-1 injury), or a Cure Disease spell cast at a -5 penalty. If the host dies to this effect, the egg hatches into a xill that eats its way out.Planewalk (10): The xill can slip into the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane and the other way around as per Jumper (p. item.title: Book of Infinite Spells
item.description: Book of Infinite SpellsThis work bestows upon any character the ability to use the spells within its pages. However, any character not already able to use spells gains has -1 to ST, DX, IQ, and HT for as long as the book is in her possession or while she uses its power. A book of infinite spells contains 2d+22 pages. The nature of each page is determined by a 1d roll: 1-3, arcane spell; 4-6, divine spell.Determine the exact spell randomly.Once a page is turned, it can never be flipped back—paging through a book of infinite spells is a one-way trip. If the book is closed, it always opens again to the page it was on before the book was closed. When the last page is turned, the book vanishes.Once per day the owner of the book can cast the spell to which the book is opened. If that spell happens to be one that the character can cast via her own spellcasting abilities, she can cast it up to four times per day. The pages cannot be ripped out without destroying the book. Similarly, the spells cannot be cast as scroll spells, nor can they be copied into a spellbook—their magic is bound up permanently within the book itself.The owner of the book need not have the book on her person in order to use its power. The book can be stored in a place of safety while the owner is adventuring and still allow its owner to cast spells by means of its power.Each time a spell is cast, there is a chance that the energy connected with its use causes the page to magically turn despite all precautions. The owner knows this and may even benefit from the turning by gaining access to a new spell. The chance of a page turning depends on the spell the page contains and what sort of spellcaster the owner is. | Condition | Chance of Page Turning (on 2d roll) | | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | | Caster employing a spell that she can cast via her own spellcasting abilities | 2 | | Caster employing a spell that she cannot cast normally | 2-3 | | Nonspellcaster employing a divine spell | 2-4 | | Nonspellcaster employing an arcane spell | 2-5 |

item.title: Libram of Ineffable Damnation
item.description:
Libram of Ineffable Damnation: This mystic book is of great value to arcane spellcasters of evil alignment (LE, NE, CE). Study of the work requires one week. Upon completion, the evil arcane caster gains a +1 inherent bonus to the ability score controlling his or her arcane spell-casting ability and experience points sufficient to place him or her halfway into the next level of experience. (If the reader has levels in more than one arcane spellcasting class, he or she must choose one of the classes to be affected.) Nonevil arcane spellcasters (LN, N, CN, LG, NG, or CG) are permanently drained of 1d4+1 points of Constitution and must atone (see the atonement spell) in order to gain any further experience. Anyone incapable of casting arcane spells who reads even a single word of the work must make a Will save (DC 20) or suffer insanity (see the insanity spell). Except as indicated above, the writing in a libram of ineffable damnation can’t be distinguished from any other book, libram, tome, or so on until perused. Once read, the book vanishes, never to be seen again, nor can the same character ever benefit from reading a similar tome a second time.
Caster Level: 19th; Weight: 3 lb.

item.title: Mirror of Opposition
item.description: Mirror of Opposition – as an enchanted item (using Sorcery)This item resembles a normal mirror about 4 feet long and 3 feet wide. It can be hung or placed on a surface and then activated by speaking a command word. Keeping the mirror active costs 1 FP per minute. The same command word deactivates the mirror. If a creature sees its reflection in the mirror’s surface while being within 8 yards of the mirror, roll a Quick Contest of Will between the creature and the mirror’s user. If the creature loses, an exact duplicate of that creature comes into being. This opposite immediately attacks the original. The duplicate has all the possessions and powers of its original (including magic). Upon the defeat or destruction of either the duplicate or the original, the duplicate and her items disappear completely. The mirror functions up to four times per day.Statistics: Affliction 1 (Will; Area Effect, 8 yards, +150%; Aura, +80%; Based on Will, +20%; Costs Fatigue, 1 FP, -5%; Disadvantage, Enemy (Evil Twin; Hunter; Constantly), +40%; Extended Duration, Permanent, +150%; Limited Use, 4/day, -20%; Magical, -10%; Malediction 1, +100%; Melee Attack, Reach C, -30%; No Signature, +20%; Requires a command word, -10%; Vision-Based, -20%) [57]. item.title: Vacuous Grimoire
item.description: Vacuous Grimoire – as an enchanted item (using Sorcery)A book of this sort looks like a normal one on some mildly interesting topic. Any character who opens the work and reads so much as a single word therein must make a Will roll. If he fails, he gets a -1 penalty to IQ that can only be removed by casting Remove Curse and burning the book. If the grimoire is placed with other books, its appearance instantly alters to conform to the look of those other works.Statistics: Affliction 1 (Will; Attribute Penalty, IQ-1, +10%; Aura, +80%; Based on Will, +20%; Cosmic, Immune to Dispel Magic, +50%; Extended Duration, Permanent, +150%; Malediction 1, +100%; Melee Attack, Reach C, -30%; No Signature, +20%; Magical -10%; Vision-Based, -20%) [47]. item.title: Bead of Force
item.description: The bead of force is a one-use item that deals explosive force damage and encloses the target in an immovable force sphere. Expensive for a one-shot item.Bead of Force – as an enchanted item (using Sorcery)This small SM-8 black sphere can be thrown up to STx3.5 yards. When the sphere arrives at the end of its trajectory, it detonates with explosive force, dealing 3d crushing damage (on a miss, check for scatter; see p. B414), affecting both substantial and insubstantial targets. The target takes damage normally; anything nearby receives “collateral damage” equal to basic damage divided (2 x the distance in yards from the blast).If a direct hit was landed, then the target becomes encircled by a shimmering force globe, just like a spherical Force Dome. The sphere contains its subject for 1 minute. Unlike Force Dome, this barrier allows air to pass, so the subject may breathe freely. The subject may struggle, but the sphere cannot be physically moved either by people outside it or by the struggles of those within. The subject is protected by the sphere – the sphere has DR 6.Most targets resist by moving fast enough to get out – use the higher of DX or twice Basic Speed, DR provides no bonuses. Someone capable of an active defense involving teleportation or insubstantiality may choose to rely on that instead; this is a resistance roll using the controlling score, not an active defense roll.            Statistics: Crushing Attack 3d (Affects Insubstantial, +20%; Explosion 2, +100%; Increased 1/2D, x10, +15%; Increased Range, x3.5, +20%; Limited Use, 1 use (1 shot), Slow Reload, -25%; Link, +10%; Magical, -10%; Muscle-Powered Range, -10%) [36] + Affliction 1 (DX or other; Based on DX, +20%; Cosmic, Irresistible Attack, +300%; Fixed Duration, +0%; Increased 1/2D, x10, +15%; Increased Range, x3.5, +20%; Limited Use, 1 use (1 shot), Slow Reload, -25%; Link, +10%; Magical, -10%; Muscle-Powered Range, -10%; Nuisance Effect, Multiple ways to resist, -10%; Paralysis, Variant, +150%; Reduced Duration, 1/3, -10%) [55]. On command, the cloak transports the wearer to the space between worlds and makes him intangible, passing through solid objects as though they weren’t there. In this state the wearer makes no noise when he moves. The wearer can perceive the tangible world, and speak normally to those within it, but he cannot pick up normal objects or affect them in any way.Physical and energy attacks cannot harm the wearer, but he is still vulnerable to psionic and (nonmaterial) magical attacks. Likewise, his physical and energy attacks cannot affect physical opponents. His psi abilities and magic spells can affect the physical world.Although the wearer can pass through solids, he must still breathe. When moving through a solid object, treat this as if he was swimming underwater for purposes of suffocation. He cannot materialize inside a solid object.The wearer can carry objects up to his light encumbrance while insubstantial, including clothing and armor. They become physical if dropped. He cannot materialize these objects inside other objects or characters.The wearer can’t disregard gravity. He must move across a horizontal surface, or along a slope that wouldn’t require Climbing rolls. item.title: Crystal Ball
item.description:
Crystal Ball – as an enchanted item (using Sorcery)This is the most common form of scrying device, a crystal sphere about 6 inches in diameter. A character can use the device to see over a distance of up to 570 miles. It is identical to the Scrying spell, but it takes 1 minute to use.
            Statistics: Scrying 16 (Immediate Preparation Required, 1 minute, -30%) [130]. Gem, x0.4; 52 EP.            TL3 Price: 2 x ($2,000 + 52 x $320) = $37,280.TL8 Price: 2 x ($30,000 + 52 x $1,180) = $182,720.Crystal Ball – as a metatronic generator (using Pyramid 3-46)

item.title: Cube of Frost Resistance
item.description: Cube of Frost ResistanceCube of Frost Resistance – as an enchanted item (using Sorcery)This cube is activated or deactivated by pressing one side. When activated, it creates a cube-shaped area 4 yards on a side centered on the possessor (or on the cube itself, if the item is later placed on a surface). The temperature within this area increases at a rate of 2°F per second up to the maximum increase of 20°F. The field absorbs all cold-based attacks as ablative DR 20. Lost DR “heals” at the rate of 1 per day. The usage drains FP at a rate of 1 per minute.Statistics: Damage Resistance 20 (Ablative, -80%; Affects Others, +50%; Area Effect, 4 yards, +100%; Costs 1 FP, -5%; Force Field, +20%; Limited, Cold, -40%; Link, +10%; Magical, -10%; Visible, -10%) [135] + Temperature Control 1 (Emanation, -20%; Heat, -50%; Link, +10%; Magical, -10%) [2]. Cube, x0.5; 69 EP.            TL3 Price: 2 x ($5,000 + 69 x $320) = $54,160.TL8 Price: 2 x ($100,000 + 69 x $1,180) = $362,840.Cube of Frost Resistance – as a metatronic generator (using Pyramid 3-46)This device is about ¾ inch across and can be made of ivory, bone, or any hard mineral. It enables its possessor to put up a special force wall 4 yards on a side around her person. This cubic screen moves with the character and provides semi-ablative DR 10. When an attack strikes this screen, every 10 points of basic damage rolled removes one point of DR, regardless of whether the attack penetrates DR. Lost DR “heals” as at a rate of 1 per day. The possessor presses one face of the cube to activate a particular type of screen or to deactivate the device. The usage drains FP at a rate of 1 per minute.            Statistics: Damage Resistance 20 (Ablative, -80%; Affects Others, +50%; Apparatus, +0%; Area Effect, 4 yards, +100%; Costs 1 FP, -5%; Force Field, +20%; Limited, Cold, -40%; Link, +10%; Magical, -10%; Visible, -10%) [135] + Temperature Control 1 (Apparatus, +0%; Emanation, -20%; Heat, -50%; Link, +10%; Magical, -10%) [2].TL3 Cost: 2 x 137 x $175 = $47,950.TL8 Cost: 2 x 137 x $3,500 = $959,000.

item.title: Decantur of Endless Water
item.description:
Decanter of Endless Water – as an enchanted item (using Sorcery)If the stopper is removed from this ordinary-looking flask and a command word spoken, an amount of fresh or salt water pours out. Separate command words determine the type as well as the volume and velocity. Effectively, this magic item can duplicate the effects of the Create Water 1 (no casting roll required) and Water Jet 2 spells (use Liquid Projector (Water Cannon) to hit).
Statistics: Create Water 1 (Cosmic, No die roll required, +100%; Magical, -10%; Reduced Fatigue Cost 1, +20%; Requires a command word, -10%) [10 / 5 = 2] + Water Jet 2 (Requires a command word, -10%) [40]. item.title: Ioun Stone (Clear Spindle)
item.description: Ioun Stone (Clear Spindle) – as an enchanted item (using Sorcery)These crystalline stones always float in the air and must be within 3 feet of their owner to be of any use. When a character first acquires a stone, she must hold it and then release it, whereupon it takes up a circling orbit 1d/2 feet from her head. Thereafter, a stone must be grasped or netted to separate it from its owner. The owner may voluntarily seize and stow a stone (to keep it safe while she is sleeping, for example), but she loses the benefits of the stone during that time. Ioun stones have DR 1, 3 hit points, and SM-8. An enemy can snatch one with an unopposed DX roll. Each ioun stone drains 1 FP per hour.The clear spindle sustains the creature without food or water.            Statistics: Doesn’t Eat or Drink (Magical, -10%) [9]. Usually On. item.title: Mirror of
item.description:
Aura strong necromancy; CL 15th; Slot —; Price 92,000 gp; Weight 45 lbs.DESCRIPTION
This item resembles a normal mirror about 4 feet long and 3 feet wide. It can be hung or placed on a surface and then activated by speaking a command word. The same command word deactivates the mirror. If a creature sees its reflection in the mirror’s surface, an exact duplicate of that creature comes into being. This opposite immediately attacks the original. The duplicate has all the possessions and powers of its original (including magic). Upon the defeat or destruction of either the duplicate or the original, the duplicate and its items disappear completely. The mirror functions up to four times per day. Destroying the mirror (Hardness 1, 5 hit points) causes all of the duplicates to immediately vanish.CONSTRUCTION REQUIREMENTS

item.title: Nolzur's Marvelous Pigments
item.description: Marvelous Pigments – as an enchanted item (using Sorcery)These magic emulsions enable their possessor to create actual, permanent objects simply by depicting their form in two dimensions. The pigments are applied by a stick tipped with bristles, hair, or fur. The emulsion flows from the application to form the desired object as the artist concentrates on the finished image. One pot of marvelous pigments is sufficient to create a 1,000-cubic-foot object by depicting it two-dimensionally over a 100-square-foot surface. The total weight of created objects must not be higher than 1 ton.Only normal, inanimate objects can be created. Creatures can’t be created. The pigments must be applied to a surface. It takes 10 minutes, 2 FP, and a successful Artist (Painting) roll to depict an object with the pigments. Marvelous pigments cannot create magic items. Objects of value depicted by the pigments — precious metals, gems, jewelry, ivory, and so on— appear to be valuable but are really made of tin, lead, paste, brass, bone, and other such inexpensive materials. The user can create normal weapons, armor, and any other mundane item (including foodstuffs) whose value does not exceed $9,000.Items created are not magical; the effect is instantaneous.    Statistics: Snatcher (Creation, +100%; Immediate Preparation Required, 10 minutes, -45%; Large Items, +50%; Magical, -10%; More Weight, 1 ton, +80%; Permanent, +300%; Specialized, Only mundane items, -15%) [448]. item.description: Scarab of Protection – as an enchanted item (using Sorcery)This device appears to be a silver medallion in the shape of a beetle. If it is held for 5 seconds, an inscription appears on its surface letting the holder know that it is a protective device. The scarab’s possessor gains Magic Resistance 3 (Improved) (p. B67). item.description: Slippers of Spider Climbing – as a metatronic generator (using Pyramid 3-46)These shoes (LTIA, page 16) enable movement on vertical surfaces or even upside down along ceilings, leaving the wearer’s hands free. item.description: Slaying Arrow (Monster Type)Slaying Arrow (Monster Type) – as an enchanted item (using Sorcery)This arrow carries a follow-up Affliction. item.title: Arms & Equipment Guide Poisons
item.description: This post describes the conversions of poisons from Arms and Equipment Guide for D&D 3.0.Aboleth OilA living victim that makes contact with aboleth oil, must make an immediate HT roll to resist. If they fail, 10 minutes later they lose their ability to breathe air and gain the ability to breathe water for margin of failure minutes. Being washed off with cool, fresh water during the onset period negates the effect. Form: Contact Poison. Cost: $690 (singular); $250 (5-batched). Recipe: $69; 4 days; defaults to Poisons-3. Statistics: Affliction 1 (HT; Advantage, Alternate Form (same template, but with Doesn’t Breathe (Gills; underwater only)); +150%; Contact Poison, -5%; Onset, 10 minutes, -10%; Terminal Condition, Cool, fresh water, -10%) [23].Adlevine Extract This poison is extracted from a tropical vine. A living victim who ingests the poison must make a HT roll after 10 minutes or suffer 1d-1 toxic damage. Every minute for 6 more cycles he must make another HT roll to resist or take the same amount of damage. After losing 1/2 HP to this poison, the victim gains a -4 penalty to IQ until he heals above this threshold. Form: Ingested Poison. Cost: $180 (singular); $65 (5-batched). Recipe: $18; 1 day; defaults to Poisons-1. Statistics: Toxic Attack 1d-1 (Cyclic, 1 minute, 6 cycles, Resistible, +120%; Ingested Poison, -85%; Onset, 10 minutes, -10%; Resistible, HT, -30%; Symptoms, 1/2 HP, -4 IQ, +80%) [6].Alforna This is a quite weak herbal poison. A living victim must make an immediate HT roll or suffer 1d-2 fatigue damage. Form: Follow-Up Poison. Cost: $60 (singular); $20 (5-batched). Recipe: $6; 1 day; defaults to Poisons-1. Statistics: Fatigue Attack 1d-2 (Follow-Up Poison, -20%; Resistible, HT, -30%) [2].Anemis Anemis is a contact poison derived from a mineral. A living victim must make an immediate HT-1 roll or suffer 1d-2 toxic damage. Every minute for 8 more cycles he must make another HT-1 roll to resist or take the same amount of damage.  After losing 1/2 HP to this poison, the victim gains a -8 penalty to ST until he heals above this threshold. Form: Contact Poison. Cost: $210 (singular); $75 (5-batched). Recipe: $21; 1 day; defaults to Poisons-1. Statistics: Toxic Attack 1d-2 (Contact Poison, -5%; Cyclic, 1 minute, 8 cycles, Resistible, +160%; Resistible, HT-1, -25%; Symptoms, 1/2 HP, -8 ST, +80%) [7].Brain Dust This bitter-smelling dust causes the subjects to hallucinate. This poison flask can be thrown (range is STx3.5). Hitting a hard surface, it breaks, creating a cloud of poison gas in a 2-yard radius. The cloud persists for 10 seconds and may drift with the wind. Any creature that inhales the gas makes an HT roll to resist. On failure, the creature begins to hallucinate and gains a -2 penalty to IQ for margin of failure minutes. Form: Grenade. Cost: $1,080 (singular); $390 (5-batched). Recipe: $108; 8 days; defaults to Poisons-4. Statistics: Affliction 1 (HT; Area Effect, 2 yards, +50%; Attribute Penalty, -2 to IQ, +20%; Drifting, +20%; Grenade, +25%; Hallucinating, +50%; Persistent, +40%; Respiratory Agent, +50%) [36].Cretel Leaf Residue This poison is extracted from a jungle flower. A living victim who ingests the poison must make a HT-1 roll after 10 minutes or suffer 1d-1 toxic damage. Every hour for 3 more cycles he must make another HT-1 roll to resist or take the same amount of damage. After losing 1/2 HP to this poison, the victim gains a -3 penalty to HT until he heals above this threshold. Form: Ingested Poison. Cost: $60 (singular); $25 (5-batched). Recipe: $6; 1 day; defaults to Poisons-1. Statistics: Toxic Attack 1d-1 (Cyclic, 1 hour, 3 cycles, Resistible, +30%; Ingested Poison, -85%; Onset, 10 minutes, -10%; Resistible, HT-1, -25%; Symptoms, 1/2 HP, -3 HT, +30%) [2].Crippling Vine A specific vine that only grows in Eskartar produced a weakening contact poison. This victim must make an HT roll or get a -3 penalty to ST and HT for 5 hours per point of margin of failure. Form: Contact Poison. Cost: $630 (singular); $225 (5-batched). Recipe: $63; 3 days; defaults to Poisons-3. Statistics: Affliction 1 (HT; Attribute Penalty, -3 to ST and -3 to HT, +30%; Contact Poison, -5%; Extended Duration, 100x, +80%) [21].Culum Powder This poison is extracted from a bark of northern tree. A living victim who ingests the poison must make a HT-1 roll after 10 minutes or suffer 1d-1 toxic damage. Every hour for 3 more cycles he must make another HT-1 roll to resist or take the same amount of damage. After losing 1/2 HP to this poison, the victim gains a -3 penalty to DX until he heals above this threshold. Form: Ingested Poison. Cost: $90 (singular); $35 (5-batched). Recipe: $9; 1 day; defaults to Poisons-1. Statistics: Toxic Attack 1d-1 (Cyclic, 1 hour, 3 cycles, Resistible, +30%; Ingested Poison, -85%; Onset, 10 minutes, -10%; Resistible, HT-1, -25%; Symptoms, 1/2 HP, -3 DX, +60%) [3].Faralin This poison is extracted from a bark of tree that grows in moderate climate. A living victim who ingests the poison must make a HT-1 roll after 10 minutes or suffer 1d-1 toxic damage. Every hour for 3 more cycles he must make another HT-1 roll to resist or take the same amount of damage. After losing 1/2 HP to this poison, the victim gains a -3 penalty to DX and HT until he heals above this threshold. Form: Ingested Poison. Cost: $90 (singular); $35 (5-batched). item.title: Contact Poisons
item.description: Here we have contact poisons converted from D&D 3.5 Dungeon Master's Guide and Pathfinder Core Rulebook.New elixir form: Contact Poison-5% This is a contact agent poison – it goes on any weapons, works if the weapon pierces DR or hits skin or DR with the Tough Skin limitation, and lasts for one wound or three hits that are blocked, parried, or stopped by DR. Ignore weight when carried on a weapon. It takes 4 seconds to apply a dose of poison to a weapon. A dose of contact poison weighs 0.5 lb., has SM-6 and Bulk -3. This is a Mini item. Statistics: Either/Or (Contact Agent, -30%; Link, Weapon, +10%; Nuisance Effect, Wears off after three blocked hits, -5%; Takes Extra Time 2, -20% or Follow-Up Poison, -20%), -5%. Black Lotus Extract      Black lotus is a rare flower found in warm marshlands. Its extract works as a contact poison. A living victim must make an immediate HT-4 roll or suffer 1 toxic damage. Every minute for 12 more cycles he must make another HT-4 roll to resist or take the same amount of damage. After losing 1/3 HP to this poison, the victim begins experiencing severe pain (p. B428) until he heals above this threshold. Form: Contact Poison. Cost: $120 (singular); $45 (5-batched). Recipe: $12; 1 day; defaults to Poisons-1. A living victim must make an immediate HT-5 roll or suffer 1d-2 toxic damage. Every minute for 8 more cycles he must make another HT-5 roll to resist or take the same amount of damage. After losing 1/2 HP to this poison, the victim gains a -8 penalty to ST until he heals above this threshold. item.title: Desert Poisons and Diseases
item.description: This post converts poisons and diseases from Sandstorm for D&D 3.5 Crystal Scorpion Poison Distilled from the venom of monstrous scorpions, this alchemically treated poison is often sought out by warlords or assassins who want to see a victim suffer for days. The process of treating the venom renders it translucent, but with the refractive qualities of a perfect prism when held up to the light in a clear container. This victim must make an HT roll or be paralyzed for 5 hours per point of margin of failure. Form: Contact Poison. Cost: $990 (singular); $360 (5-batched). Recipe: $99; 6 days; defaults to Poisons-4. Statistics: Affliction 1 (HT; Contact Poison, -5%; Extended Duration, 100x, +80%; Paralysis, +150%) [33].Volcanic Gas Active volcano craters, mud pots, and similar features often vent a poisonous mixture of gases. This is a respiratory agent. This poison flask can be thrown (range is STx3.5). Hitting a hard surface, it breaks, creating a cloud of poison gas in a 2-yard radius. The cloud persists for 10 seconds and may drift with the wind. Any creature that inhales the gas must make an immediate HT roll or suffer 1d-2 fatigue damage. Every 10 seconds for 4 more cycles he must make another HT roll to resist or take the same amount of damage. Form: Grenade. Cost: $450 (singular); $160 (5-batched). Recipe: $45; 2 days; defaults to Poisons-2. Statistics: Fatigue Attack 1d-2 (Area Effect, 2 yards, +50%; Drifting, +20%; Cyclic, 10 second, 4 cycles, Resistible, +100%; Grenade, +25%; Persistent, +40%; Resistible, HT, -30%; Respiratory Agent, +50%) [15]. Sandeyes A creeping blindness caused by desiccated eye tissue. Statistics: Contact; HT-1 to resist; 1 day delay; 1d-2 toxic damage (with Blindness after loss of 2/3 HP; if the victim loses all his HP, he becomes blinded permanently); 24-hour cycle with six cycles. Mildly contagious.Volcanic Fever This disease spreads through the inhalation of ash, which causes the victim’s body temperature to rise to an unearthly heat. A character killed by volcanic fever crumbles into fine ash within 24 hours. Statistics: Respiratory; HT-2 to resist; 1d/2 days delay; 1d-2 toxic damage (with ST-2 and DX-2 after loss of 1/3 HP; DX-4, ST-4, HT-4 after loss of ½ HP; and agony after loss of 2/3 HP); 12-hour cycle with six cycles. Not contagious.Wasting, The This is a supernatural disease spread by demons and other foul creatures of the waste. Skin and tissues slowly dry and toughen, mummifying the victim. Statistics: Blood; HT-3 to resist; 1 day delay; 1d-1 toxic damage (with DX-2 after loss of 1/3 HP; DX-4 after loss of ½ HP; and Numb and terrible pain after loss of 2/3 HP); 12-hour cycle with ten cycles. Not contagious.Source: https://enragedeggplant.blogspot.com/2018/11/alchemy-desert-poisons-and-diseases.html?m=0

Statistics: Toxic Attack 1d-1 (Contact Poison, -5%; Cyclic, 1 minute, 3 cycles, Resistible, +60%; Resistible, HT-1, -25%; Symptoms, 1/3 HP, -2 to HT, +30%; Symptoms, 1/2 HP, -4 to HT, +40%) [6].

item.title: Drow Poisons
item.description: Let's convert the normal, not magic-infused poisons from Drow of the Underdark. Darklight Brew Darklight ore is powdered and cut with a mild acid to create this poison. The radiation of the ore is diminished greatly in this process, but its effect becomes acute when it is introduced into the bloodstream. A living victim must make an immediate HT-2 roll or suffer 1d-1 toxic damage. Every second for 4 more cycles he must make another HT-2 roll to resist or take the same amount of damage. After losing 1/2 HP to this poison, the victim becomes blinded until he heals above this threshold. Form: Follow-Up Poison. Cost: $330 (singular); $120 (5-batched). Recipe: $33; 1 day; defaults to Poisons-2. Statistics: Toxic Attack 1d-1 (Cyclic, 1 second, 4 cycles, Resistible, +200%; Follow-Up Poison, -20%; Resistible, HT-2, -20%; Symptoms, 1/2 HP, Blindness, +100%) [11]. Fish Glue The body oil of captured kuo-toas is used to create this poison, which is named for the rigidity it causes in the joints of the victim and its characteristic fishy smell. The victim must resist with HT or become nauseated and get a -4 penalty to DX for margin of failure minutes. Form: Follow-Up Poison. Cost: $450 (singular); $160 (5-batched). Recipe: $45; 2 days; defaults to Poisons-2. Statistics: Affliction 1 (HT; Attribute Penalty, DX-4, +40%; Follow-Up Poison, -20%; Nauseated, +30%) [15].    Illithid Mindscorch The brain matter of recently slain illithids can be distilled, capturing some of its psionic potential and creating this extremely rare poison. Though it is a liquid in its basic form, it is ineffective unless reduced to an aerosol and absorbed through the nasal passages of the victim. This poison flask can be thrown (range is STx3.5). Hitting a hard surface, it breaks, creating a cloud of poison gas in a 2-yard radius. The cloud persists for 10 seconds and may drift with the wind. Any creature that inhales the gas makes an HT roll to resist. On failure, the creature takes -4 to IQ for 1 minute. Form: Grenade. Cost: $930 (singular); $335 (5-batched). Recipe: $93; 5 days; defaults to Poisons-4. Statistics: Affliction 1 (HT; Area Effect, 2 yards, +50%; Attribute Penalty, -3 to IQ, +30%; Drifting, +20%; Fixed Duration, +0%; Grenade, +25%; Persistent, +40%; Reduced Duration, 1/3, -10%; Respiratory Agent, +50%) [31]. Psychotropic Rot Distilled violet fungus and other chemicals can be mixed together to create this insidious toxin. A living victim who ingests the poison must make a HT roll after 10 minutes or suffer 1d-1 toxic damage. Every minute for 6 more cycles he must make another HT roll to resist or take the same amount of damage. After losing 1/2 HP to this poison, the victim gains a -2 penalty to IQ until he heals above this threshold. Form: Ingested Poison. Cost: $150 (singular); $55 (5-batched). Recipe: $15; 1 day; defaults to Poisons-1. Statistics: Toxic Attack 1d-1 (Cyclic, 1 minute, 6 cycles, Resistible, +120%; Ingested Poison, -85%; Onset, 10 minutes, -10%; Resistible, HT, -30%; Symptoms, 1/2 HP, -2 IQ, +40%) [5].    Roach Paste This brown paste is made from the crushed bodies of the carrion-eating giant roaches found in the Underdark. It is known for its horrendous smell. The victim must resist with HT or become nauseated for margin of failure seconds. Regardless of the result of this HT roll, two days later the victim must make an HT-2 roll to avoid contracting filth fever. Filth fever is a disease that deals 1d-2 toxic damage each 12 hours for 12 cycles. Each instance of damage can be resisted with a HT-2 roll. After losing 1/3 HP to this disease, the victim gets a -2 penalty to DX and HT until he heals above this threshold. Form: Follow-Up Poison. Cost: $420 (singular); $150 (5-batched). Recipe: $42; 1 day; defaults to Poisons-2. Statistics: Affliction 1 (HT; Follow-Up Poison, -20%; Link, +10%; Nauseated, +30%; Reduced Duration, 1/60, -35%) [9] + Toxic Attack 1d-2 (Follow-Up Poison, -20%; Link, +10%; Resistible, HT-2, -20%; Onset, 2 days, -30%; Cyclic, 12-hour cycle with 12 cycles, +120%; Symptoms, 1/3 HP, DX-2, HT-2, +90%) [5].Underdark Blight Running a chemical solution over certain rare ores and minerals found in the Underdark creates this poison; it is effective at removing magic resistance. A living victim must make an immediate HT-3 roll or suffer 1 toxic damage. Every second for 9 more cycles he must make another HT-3 roll to resist or take the same amount of damage. After losing 1/3 HP to this poison, the victim gains Magic Susceptibility 2 (p. B143) or has his Magic Resistance decreased by 2 until he heals above this threshold. Form: Contact Poison. Cost: $180 (singular); $65 (5-batched). Recipe: $18; 1 day; defaults to Poisons-1. Statistics: Toxic Attack 1 (Contact Poison, -5%; Cosmic, Compatible with Magic Resistance, +50%; Cyclic, 1 seconds, 9 cycles, Resistible, +450%; Resistible, HT-3, -15%; Symptoms, 1/3 HP, Magic Susceptibility 2, +20%) [6].Source: https://enragedeggplant.blogspot.com/2020/12/alchemy-drow-poisons.html?m=0

item.title: Dungeon Concoctions VI
item.description: Here we have the last potions and poisons from GURPS Dungeon Fantasy 14 - Psi with the exclusion of spice.Bloque This potion can be thrown (range is STx3.5). Hitting a hard surface, it breaks, creating a cloud of fumes in a 2-yard radius that obstruct a specific ESP or Telepathy ability, Telekinesis, or a particular psionic attack. That ability cannot penetrate the fumes at all – if the line of sight from psi to target crosses the area, the attempt fails. Everything inside the area is immune (senses perceive an impenetrable cloud). Duration: 1d minutes. Form: Grenade. Cost: $1,440 (singular); $520 (5-batched). Recipe: $144; 12 days; defaults to Alchemy (Psionic)-5. Statistics: Static (Psi; Area Effect, 2 yards, +50%; Extended Duration, 30x, +60%; Grenade, +0%; Magical, -10%; One Ability, -80%; Ranged, +40%) [48].Pshield The subject gains a +3 bonus to IQ and Will rolls made to resist psionics for 1 hour. Duration: 1 hour. Form: Potion. Cost: $480 (singular); $170 (5-batched). Recipe: $48; 2 days; defaults to Alchemy (Psionic)-2. Statistics: Affliction 1 (HT; Advantage, Pshield, +90%; Magical, -10%; Potion, -25%) [16]. Notes: «Pshield» is Resistant to Psionics (+3) (Magical, -10%) [9].Pslay This blade venom has no effect on most targets. A psi must make a HT roll at a penalty equal to Psi Talent. Failure means 2d toxic injury. Form: Follow-Up Poison. Cost: $120 (singular); $45 (5-batched). Recipe: $12; 4 days; defaults to Poisons-1. Statistics: Toxic Attack 2d (Accessibility, Only on psis, -20%; Follow-Up Poison, -20%; Resistible, HT, Extra penalty, -20%) [4].Pslay BR This blade venom has no effect on most targets. A psi must make a HT roll at a penalty equal to Psi Talent. Failure means 6d toxic injury. Form: Follow-Up Poison. Cost: $300 (singular); $110 (5-batched). Recipe: $30; 1 day; defaults to Poisons-1. Statistics: Toxic Attack 6d (Accessibility, Only on psis, -20%; Follow-Up Poison, -20%; Resistible, HT, Extra penalty, -20%) [10].Source: https://enragedeggplant.blogspot.com/2018/09/alchemy-dungeon-concoctions-vi.html?m=0

item.title: Dungeon Poisons
item.description:
My Metatronic Alchemy system can be used to craft poisons, just replace the Alchemy skill with Poisons. Here we have two follow-up poisons and two grenade poisons from GURPS Dungeon Fantasy 1 - Adventurers presented as metatronic elixirs. The costs difference between two variants varies from "slightly" to "a lot".NEW FORMFollow-Up Poison-20%This is a follow-up agent poison – it goes on cutting or impaling weapons, works only if the blade pierces DR, and lasts for one wound or three hits that are blocked, parried, or stopped by DR. Ignore weight when carried on a weapon. It takes 4 seconds to apply a dose of poison to a weapon. Alternatively, this poison may be swallowed or mixed with food or drink. Once in hand, it takes a Ready maneuver to open the vial, another to drink. One dose of ingested poison affects one man-sized creature instantly. A dose of follow-up poison weighs 0.5 lb., has SM-6 and Bulk -3. This is a Mini item.Statistics: Either/Or (Follow-Up, Weapon, +0%; Nuisance Effect, Wears off after three blocked hits, -5%; Takes Extra Time 2, -20% or Blood Agent, -40%; Can be mixed with food, +5%; Melee Attack, Reach C, Cannot Parry, -35%; Takes Extra Time 1, -10%), -20% POISONSBladeblackDeadliest manmade blade venom, from the legendary Assassins’ Guild. A living victim must make an immediate HT-5 roll or suffer 6d toxic damage.Form: Follow-Up Poison.Cost: $540 (singular); $195 (5-batched).Recipe: $54; 2 days; defaults to Poisons-2.Statistics: Toxic Attack 6d (Follow-Up Poison, -20%; Resistible, HT-5, -5%) [18].Demon BrewThis is a respiratory agent made from demon ichor. This poison flask can be thrown (range is STx3.5). Hitting a hard surface, it breaks, creating a cloud of poison gas in a 2-yard radius. The cloud persists for 10 seconds and may drift with the wind. Any creature that inhales the gas makes an HT roll to resist. If the roll is successful, the creature takes 1d toxic damage; if the roll is failed, the creature takes 2d toxic damage.Form: Grenade.Cost: $690 (singular); $250 (5-batched).Recipe: $69; 3 days; defaults to Poisons-3.Statistics: Toxic Attack 1d (HT; Area Effect, 2 yards, +50%; Drifting, +20%; Fixed Duration, +0%; Grenade, +25%; Link, +10%; Persistent, +40%; Respiratory Agent, +50%) [12] + Toxic Attack 1d (HT; Area Effect, 2 yards, +50%; Drifting, +20%; Fixed Duration, +0%; Grenade, +25%; Link, +10%; Persistent, +40%; Resistible, HT, -30%; Respiratory Agent, +50%) [11].Monster DroolGeneric blade venom made from giant centipedes, spiders, or whatever else is in season. Often used on whole quivers of arrows because it is cheap. A living victim must make an immediate HT roll or suffer 2 points of toxic damage.Form: Follow-Up Poison.Cost: $30 (singular); $10 (5-batched).Recipe: $3; 1 day; defaults to Poisons-1.Statistics: Toxic Attack 2 (Follow-Up Poison, -20%; Resistible, HT, -30%) [1].Oozing DoomThis is a contact agent made from slimes. This poison flask can be thrown (range is STx3.5). Hitting a hard surface, it breaks, creating a cloud of poison gas in a 2-yard radius. The cloud persists for 10 seconds and may drift with the wind. Any unsealed creature in the gas makes an HT roll to resist. If the roll is successful, the creature takes 1d toxic damage; if the roll is failed, the creature takes 2d toxic damage.Form: Grenade.Cost: $930 (singular); $335 (5-batched).Recipe: $93; 5 days; defaults to Poisons-4.Statistics: Toxic Attack 1d (HT; Area Effect, 2 yards, +50%; Contact Agent, +150%; Drifting, +20%; Fixed Duration, +0%; Grenade, +25%; Link, +10%; Persistent, +40%) [16] + Toxic Attack 1d (HT; Area Effect, 2 yards, +50%; Contact Agent, +150%; Drifting, +20%; Fixed Duration, +0%; Grenade, +25%; Link, +10%; Persistent, +40%; Resistible, HT, -30%) [15].
Source: https://enragedeggplant.blogspot.com/2018/02/alchemy-dungeon-poisons.html

item.title: Dungeon Poisons II
item.description:
GURPS Dungeon Fantasy 8 - Treasure Tables has three new poisons. Here are their conversions to the Metatronic Alchemy system.BaneRather than a specific poison, this is actually a series of poisons, each of which targets a specific race or type of monster. Others suffer no ill effects (for example, elves are harmed by elfbane but take no damage from dwarfbane, while the opposite is true of dwarves). A living victim of the appropriate must make an immediate HT roll to resist. He takes 3d toxic damage on a failed roll or 1d+1 on a successful roll.Form: Follow-Up Poison.Cost: $150 (singular); $55 (5-batched).Recipe: $15; 1 day; defaults to Poisons-1.Statistics: Toxic Attack 2d-1 (Accessibility, Only on creatures of the appropriate type, -40%; Follow-Up Poison, -20%; Link, +10%; Resistible, HT, -30%) [2] + Toxic Attack 1d+1 (Accessibility, Only on creatures of the appropriate type, -40%; Follow-Up Poison, -20%; Link, +10%) [3].Fire ToxinThis poison does little actual damage but causes lasting pain. Roll vs. HT or suffer from severe pain (see p. B428) for a half-hour. On a critical failure or a failure by 5 or more, the pain increases to terrible.Form: Follow-Up Poison.Cost: $540 (singular); $195 (5-batched).Recipe: $54; 2 days; defaults to Poisons-2.Statistics: Affliction 1 (HT; Fixed Duration, +0%; Extended Duration, 10x, +40%; Follow-Up Poison, -20%; Secondary Terrible Pain, +12%; Severe Pain, +40%) [18].Knockout GasThis is a respiratory agent made from giant-lotus pollen. This poison flask can be thrown (range is STx3.5). Hitting a hard surface, it breaks, creating a cloud of poison gas in a 2-yard radius. The cloud persists for 10 seconds and may drift with the wind. Any creature that inhales the gas makes an HT roll to resist. On failure, the creature becomes drowsy (see p. B428) for a half-hour (roll vs. Will to remain conscious at the end of the period). On a failure by 5 or more or a critical failure, the target falls asleep instead. He can be woken up normally after 30 minutes have passed.Form: Grenade.Cost: $1,140 (singular); $410 (5-batched).Recipe: $114; 8 days; defaults to Poisons-4.Statistics: Affliction 1 (HT; Area Effect, 2 yards, +50%; Drifting, +20%; Drowsy, +20%; Fixed Duration, +0%; Extended Duration, 10x, +40%; Grenade, +25%; Persistent, +40%; Respiratory Agent, +50%; Secondary Sleep, +30%) [38].
Source: https://enragedeggplant.blogspot.com/2018/02/alchemy-dungeon-poisons-ii.html?m=0

item.title: Dungeon Poisons III
item.description:
GURPS Dungeon Fantasy 12 - Ninja gives us three more poisons to work with. Here's my take on converting them to the Metatronic Alchemy system.Blinding GasThis is a contact agent made from assorted natural irritant powders. This poison flask can be thrown (range is STx3.5). Hitting a hard surface, it breaks, creating a cloud of poison gas in a 2-yard radius. The cloud persists for 10 seconds and may drift with the wind. Any unsealed creature with unprotected eyes in the gas makes an HT roll to resist. On a failed roll, the victim becomes blind for a number of minutes equal to the margin of failure. If the victim can wash out all of his eyes (takes five seconds and an available water source), the blindness ends immediately.Form: Grenade.Cost: $1,230 (singular); $445 (5-batched).Recipe: $123; 9 days; defaults to Poisons-5.Statistics: Affliction 1 (HT; Area Effect, 2 yards, +50%; Contact Agent, +150%; Disadvantage, Blindness, +50%; Drifting, +20%; Grenade, +25%; Persistent, +40%; Terminal Condition, Washing out, -10%; Vision-Based, -20%) [41].Mind FogThis is a respiratory agent made from burned laquer. This poison flask can be thrown (range is STx3.5). Hitting a hard surface, it breaks, creating a cloud of poison gas in a 2-yard radius. The cloud persists for 10 seconds and may drift with the wind. Any creature that inhales the gas makes an HT roll to resist. On failure, the creature becomes dizzy and confused: it takes -3 to DX and IQ for 1 minute.Form: Grenade.Cost: $1,020 (singular); $365 (5-batched).Recipe: $102; 6 days; defaults to Poisons-4.Statistics: Affliction 1 (HT; Area Effect, 2 yards, +50%; Attribute Penalty, -3 to DX and IQ, +60%; Drifting, +20%; Fixed Duration, +0%; Grenade, +25%; Persistent, +40%; Reduced Duration, 1/3, -10%; Respiratory Agent, +50%) [34].Paralytic SlimeThis poison is a blood agent derived from a mix of rare and deadly fungus and giant-insect venom. Roll vs. HT or be paralyzed for a number of minutes equal to the margin of failure.Form: Follow-Up Poison.Cost: $690 (singular); $250 (5-batched).Recipe: $69; 3 days; defaults to Poisons-3.Statistics: Affliction 1 (HT; Follow-Up Poison, -20%; Paralysis, +150%) [23].
Source: https://enragedeggplant.blogspot.com/2018/02/alchemy-dungeon-poisons-iii.html?m=0

item.title: Faerun Poisons
item.description: Races of Faerun, Underdark, and Serpent Kingdoms (I omitted the ossra oils - they would require a little bit different framework) for D&D 3.5 have some poisons that I have not converted to GURPS yet. The last non-Dragon Magazine poisons.   Blue Frog Paste This contact poison is secreted by otherwise harmless bright blue frogs. Lizardfolk mix it with other natural substances to produce a highly toxic oil suitable for applying to weapons. A living victim that touches the poison with bare skin must roll against HT or take a -3 penalty to DX for margin of failure minutes. If he fails by 5 or fails critically, he instead is paralyzed for margin of failure minutes. Form: Contact Poison. Cost: $480 (singular); $175 (5-batched). Recipe: $48; 2 days; defaults to Poisons-2. Statistics: Affliction 1 (HT; Attribute Penalty, DX-3, +30%; Contact Poison, -5%; Fixed Duration, +0%; Secondary Paralysis, +30%) [16].  Cave Terror This poison is distilled from cave creeper fungus. A living victim who ingests the poison must make a HT-2 roll after 10 minutes or suffer 1d toxic damage. Every minute for 6 more cycles he must make another HT-2 roll to resist or take the same amount of damage. After losing 1/2 HP to this poison, the victim gains a -4 penalty to IQ until he heals above this threshold. After losing 2/3 HP to this poison, the victim begins to hallucinate (p. B428) until he heals above this threshold. Form: Ingested Poison. Cost: $300 (singular); $110 (5-batched). Recipe: $30; 1 day; defaults to Poisons-1. Statistics: Toxic Attack 1d (Cyclic, 1 minute, 6 cycles, Resistible, +120%; Ingested Poison, -85%; Onset, 10 minutes, -10%; Resistible, HT-2, -20%; Symptoms, 1/2 HP, -4 IQ, +80%; Symptoms, 2/3 HP, Hallucinating, +50%) [10].      Sickstone Unguent This paste is made of powdered sickstone and other virulent poisons. A living victim must make an immediate HT-1 roll or suffer 1d-2 toxic damage. Every minute for 8 more cycles he must make another HT-1 roll to resist or take the same amount of damage.  After losing 1/2 HP to this poison, the victim gains a -4 penalty to HT until he heals above this threshold. Form: Contact Poison. Cost: $180 (singular); $65 (5-batched). Recipe: $18; 1 day; defaults to Poisons-1. Statistics: Toxic Attack 1d-2 (Contact Poison, -5%; Cyclic, 1 minute, 8 cycles, Resistible, +160%; Resistible, HT-1, -25%; Symptoms, 1/2 HP, -4 HT, +40%) [6].   Sleep Poison The lizardfolk have developed a technique for distilling the extract of several jungle plants to produce a poison that renders enemies unconscious. A living victim that touches the poison with bare skin must roll against HT or lose consciousness for margin of failure minutes. Form: Contact Poison. Cost: $900 (singular); $325 (5-batched). Recipe: $90; 5 days; defaults to Poisons-3. Statistics: Affliction 1 (HT; Contact Poison, -5%; Fixed Duration, +0%; Unconsciousness, +200%) [30].   Sssartisss A distillate of the venoms of several kinds of poisonous serpents, sssartisss has a bitter tang when wet and a scaled or furrowed texture when dry. A living victim must roll against HT or lose consciousness for margin of failure minutes. Form: Follow-Up Poison. Cost: $840 (singular); $305 (5-batched). Recipe: $84; 4 days; defaults to Poisons-3. Statistics: Affliction 1 (HT; Fixed Duration, +0%; Follow-Up Poison, -20%; Unconsciousness, +200%) [28].Stun Gas The svirfneblin brew this contact agent gas from the spores of rare mushrooms. This poison flask can be thrown (range is STx3.5). Hitting a hard surface, it breaks, creating a cloud of poison gas in a 2-yard radius. The cloud persists for 10 seconds and may drift with the wind. Any unsealed creature in the gas makes an HT roll to resist. On a failed roll, the victim becomes stunned and can try to recover next turn. Form: Grenade. Cost: $1,170 (singular); $420 (5-batched). Recipe: $117; 8 days; defaults to Poisons-4. Statistics: Affliction 1 (HT; Area Effect, 2 yards, +50%; Contact Agent, +150%; Drifting, +20%; Grenade, +25%; Persistent, +40%) [39].   Ts’ous This substance is a mixture of cobra venom and the extracts of several poisonous plants. It smells like overripe fruit when wet and dries clear. A living victim must make an immediate HT-1 roll or suffer 2d toxic damage. Form: Follow-Up Poison. Cost: $150 (singular); $55 (5-batched). Recipe: $15; 1 day; defaults to Poisons-1. Statistics: Toxic Attack 2d (Follow-Up Poison, -20%; Resistible, HT-1, -25%) [5].Virile Madness An admixture of rare earths and magical rocks, virile madness is a dangerous, tempting poison. It grants the imbiber a temporary +2 bonus to ST, while degrading her mental powers via a -3 penalty to IQ. Both effects last for margin of failure minutes. Form: Ingested Poison. Cost: $750 (singular); $270 (5-batched). Recipe: $75; 4 days; defaults to Poisons-3. Statistics: Affliction 1 (HT; Advantage, ST+2, +200%; Attribute Penalty, -3 to IQ, +30%; Ingested Poison, -85%) [25].    Wild Dwarf Knockout Poison Wild dwarves coat their blowgun darts with poison made from a plant. A living victim struck by a poisoned weapon must make an HT roll to avoid being stunned. If he fails by 5 or more or fails critically, he loses consciousness for margin of failure minutes instead. Form: Follow-Up Poison. Cost: $360 (singular); $130 (5-batched). Recipe: $36; 1 day; defaults to Poisons-2. Statistics: Affliction 1 (HT; Follow-Up Poison, -20%; Secondary Unconsciousness, +40%) [12].Source: https://enragedeggplant.blogspot.com/2021/09/alchemy-faerun-poisons.html?m=0

item.title: Magic Infused Poisons
item.description: One category of D&D poisons that I missed is the magic-infused poisons from Drow of the Underdark. Hopefully, I'm not missing anything else.        Poisons/TL (IQ/Hard)This skill gets the following new specialty.       Magic-Infused Poisons: This specialty covers the knowledge of magic-infused poisons – special drow-made poisons laced with magic. Prerequisite: any arcane magical abilities. Defaults: Poisons-4.The Calling This lumpy black paste is magically infused with spider eggs and can be hidden in a dish of food, in which it is detectable only with a successful Cooking roll. If it is consumed, and if the victim fails the initial HT-3 roll, a swarm of spiders hatches within the victim's stomach, dealing 2d toxic damage. The swarm is then digested and destroyed without further harm, unless 10 minutes later the second HT-3 roll is failed. In that case, it bursts forth from the victim's nose and mouth, dealing 2d toxic damage and coalescing as a spider swarm (use statistics of insect swarm from GURPS Dungeon Fantasy 5 – Allies, page 9, but replace Flight with Clinging), attacking everyone in the area. Form: Ingested Poison. Cost: $810 (singular); $290 (5-batched). Recipe: $81; 4 days; defaults to Poisons (Magic-Infused)-3. Statistics: Toxic Attack 2d (Ingested Poison, -85%; Magical, -10%; Resistible, HT-3, -15%) [4] + Toxic Attack 2d (Cosmic, Summons a swarm, +300%; Follow-Up, Initial Toxic Attack, -45%; Magical, -10%; Onset, 10 minutes, -10%; Resistible, HT-3, -15%) [27].Creeping Nullscourge This poison is used during bouts of drow infighting. A living victim must make an immediate HT-3 roll or suffer 1 toxic damage. Every second for 9 more cycles he must make another HT-3 roll to resist or take the same amount of damage. After losing 1/3 HP to this poison, the victim gains Magic Susceptibility 2 (p. B143) or has his Magic Resistance decreased by 2 until he heals above this threshold. After losing 1/2 HP to this poison, the victim gains Magic Susceptibility 4 (p. B143) or has his Magic Resistance decreased by 4 until he heals above this threshold. After losing 2/3 HP to this poison, the victim gains Magic Susceptibility 6 (p. B143) or has his Magic Resistance decreased by 6 until he heals above this threshold. Form: Follow-Up Poison. It is usually administered to a prisoner over several days; each dose creates a slower and more agonizing biting sensation similar to that caused by swarming spiderbite, but also disfigures the body with horrific red boils. After losing 1/3 HP to this poison, the victim experiences moderate pain until he heals above this threshold. After losing 2/3 HP to this poison, the victim experiences terrible pain and his Appearance shifts two steps down until he heals above this threshold. Form: Ingested Poison. item.title: Psychic Poisons
item.description: Book of Vile Darkness for D&D 3.0 introduces a new poison type that probably has barely seen use in D&D (just like normal poisons, to be honest) - psychic poisons. They are applied to creatures, objects, or areas, but affect creatures that use mental and information abilities on these creatures, objects, or areas. Thus, they are mostly defensive in nature and are very useful when fighting spellcasters and psis. I feel like they differ so much from normal poisons that they deserve a new skill specialty.Poisons/TL (IQ/Hard)            This skill gets a new specialty.Psychic Poisons: This specialty covers the knowledge of psychic poisons – special substances that poison spellcasters casting spells on creatures carrying the poison on their skin or in their blood. Defaults: Poisons-4.New form: Area Ointment Psychic Poison-85%A cream or jelly. It usually takes 1 minute to apply an ointment to an area of a 2-yard radius. Can be washed off with water. A flask with an ointment weighs 0.5 lb., has SM-6 and Bulk -3. This is a Mini item.Statistics: Area Effect, 2 yards, +50%; Fixed Duration, +0%; Immediate Preparation Required, 1 minute, -30%; Melee Attack, Reach C, Cannot Parry, -35%; Terminal Condition, Water, -10%.New form: Ointment Psychic Poison-105%A cream or jelly. It usually takes 8 seconds to apply an ointment to an object or person. Can be washed off with water. A flask with an ointment weighs 0.5 lb., has SM-6 and Bulk -3. This is a Mini item.Statistics: Contact Agent, -30%; Fixed Duration, +0%; Melee Attack, Reach C, Cannot Parry, -35%; Takes Extra Time 3, -30%; Terminal Condition, Water, -10%.POISONSDarin-TasithThis psychic poison must be applied to the subject’s skin. Applying the poison takes 8 seconds. It lasts for 5 hours or until washed off with water. Whenever another character within 128 yards targets the subject with a mind-affecting ability (such as a Mind Control spell or a Telepathy power) or an Information spell or a similar ability (for example, Detect Magic or Psi Sense), he must resist with a Quick Contest of HT against the poisoncrafter's Poisons skill, using the normal range penalties. If he fails, he takes 1d-2 toxic damage. Every second for 5 more cycles he must win in another identical Quick Contest to resist or take the same amount of damage. After losing 1/3 HP to this poison, the victim gets a -2 penalty to IQ until he heals above this threshold. If he fails, he takes 1d-1 toxic damage. Every second for 6 more cycles he must win in another identical Quick Contest to resist or take the same amount of damage.
